title: Live contract verifier for staged model rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add a lightweight, low-latency runtime verifier that validates structured response contracts and function-call interfaces during staged model rollouts. The verifier will operate in monitor and enforcement modes, support mirrored (shadow) traffic and percentage-based sampling, and emit per-route violation metrics to the Console for fast diagnostics and automated rollback triggers.
background: We frequently onboard model updates that change structured outputs or tool-call signatures. Current rollouts rely on offline diffs and ad-hoc evals; we've seen regressions where downstream tooling or customers received unexpected shapes and error paths. Existing tickets cover contract audits and post-hoc detection, but we lack a runtime guard that provides immediate visibility and automatic corrective action without requiring full traffic diversion.
proposal: Implement a "live contract verifier" component in the request path that performs three capabilities: 1) schema validation against a pinned expected JSON schema or function-call signature; 2) compact delta detection for parameter/return-type changes (signature hashes + path-level diffs); 3) configurable response handling (log-only, shadow-fail, block-and-fallback). The verifier must be pluggable per-route/model, toggleable via feature flag, and add <1ms median latency for typical responses. We will use deterministic normalization + MurmurHash to fingerprint shapes, and maintain a small cache of recent fingerprints to avoid repeated deep comparisons.
acceptance_criteria:
- Verifier can be enabled per deployment and per route via rollout config.
- Monitor mode: verifier logs violations and emits metrics (violation_count, violation_rate, top_mismatch_examples) without affecting responses.
- Enforcement mode: when violation_rate > configured_threshold for X minutes, new-variant traffic is automatically reverted to previous variant or routed to fallback model.
- Shadow mode: verifier runs on mirrored requests and stores 1000 sample mismatches per 24h per model.
- Performance overhead: p50 added latency < 1ms, p95 < 5ms under production sampler rates.
- Security review completed and KMS keys usage for storing sampled payloads where PII flagged.
implementation_notes:
- Integrate verifier as a middleware in the runtime's routing layer with async telemetry emission to the Console.
- Fingerprinting: normalize JSON (sort keys, remove floating-point noise), then compute MurmurHash64. For function-call payloads, canonicalize name+arg-types.
- Delta detection: on mismatch, compute a lightweight path-based diff (presence, type, enum differences) and store a short summary string.
- Caching: LRU cache with 4096 entries for recent fingerprints per worker to short-circuit common responses.
- Config: rollout config accepts fields: mode (monitor|enforce|shadow), sample_rate (0.0-1.0), threshold_pct, window_minutes, revert_action (route_to_previous|route_to_fallback|block), sample_storage_ttl_days.
- Telemetry: emit counters and histogram for violation latency, and tags for model_id, route, region, and customer_tier.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flagged deploy to runtime edge in monitor-only mode for internal traffic (1 day).
2) Enable shadow mode for 5% of production traffic; collect samples and validate false-positive rate (3 days).
3) Ramp sample_rate to 25% for targeted routes with high-risk tool-calls (2 days).
4) Switch to enforcement mode with conservative threshold (2%) on a small canary (5% new-variant traffic). Watch for automated revert behavior in staging exercises.
5) If metrics stable for 72h, expand enforcement to 50% then 100% per schedule.
Note: each step includes a go/no-go checkpoint with stakeholders and a 1-hour rollback window.
monitoring_and_telemetry:
- Console dashboard: per-model violation_rate, top 10 mismatch signatures, time-series of violations, sampled request/response pairs (redacted).
- Alerts: P99 violation_rate > 5% for > 30m; absolute violation_count > 1000 in 1h; auto-revert events.
- Tracing: attach verifier latency to existing request traces and annotate with mismatch code.
- Data retention: sampled mismatches retained 14 days for debugging; PII redaction rules applied before storage.
test_plan:
- Unit tests: normalization, fingerprinting, diff summarization, cache behavior.
- Integration tests: deploy verifier in a canary runtime with synthetic model variants that introduce shape mutations; assert correct metrics and revert behavior.
- Load test: simulate 10k rps with 25% sampling to verify latency targets and memory bounds.
- Chaos tests: random flakey storage and latency injection to verify graceful degradation (monitor-only fallback if verifier exceeds latency budget).
risk_and_mitigation:
- False positives: mitigate via normalization heuristics and a grace period threshold before enforcement.
- Performance overhead: mitigate with sampling, caching, and async telemetry emission.
- Privacy: sampled payloads may contain user data; apply deterministic redaction and use KMS-backed storage.
- Operator blast radius: restrict enforcement to targeted routes and require two-person approval for auto-enforce enablement in production.
rollback_playbook:
1) If automated revert triggers, notify on-call and send a summary with top mismatch examples.
2) On-call runs sanity checklist: check recent deploys, check Console revert logs, confirm traffic shifted.
3) If revert did not resolve downstream errors, escalate to runtime SRE and open an incident.
4) For manual rollback: flip feature flag to monitor-only, and if needed, deploy hotfix to model metadata (re-pin schema) before re-enabling enforcement.
updates: 2026-02-18: Spike completed — basic fingerprinting prototype implemented in a dev branch. Observed normalized fingerprint stability across small format changes.
2026-02-25: Design review with Runtime and Console teams. Agreed on telemetry schema and sample storage TTL. Security requested explicit KMS encryption for stored samples.
2026-03-04: Integration PR opened (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2913) with middleware plumbing and feature-flag gates. Unit tests added for canonicalization logic.

2026-03-10: Internal canary run on staging for 24h in monitor mode; measured p50 overhead 0.6ms and p95 4.2ms at 5% sampling. Two false-positive patterns found and addressed (timestamp formats and minor enum synonyms).
2026-03-13: Moving to shadow mode for a targeted subset of production routes at 10% sample rate. Notifying customer-facing teams and Solutions for potential downstream compatibility checks.
